text: The relationship is many‑to‑one: each post is written by one author, while an author can write many posts, so the foreign key belongs on the “many” side of the relation. In the blog example the `author = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='blog_posts')` line is added to the **Post** model, which creates a foreign‑key column in the posts table that points to the author’s primary key [1]. Placing a `ForeignKey` in the Author model would instead make each author point to a single post, reversing the intended cardinality. Therefore the correct location for the foreign key is the Post model.
